_removed_note: drop-bytecode-isolation and drop-mtime-bump both SURVIVE individually because the two invalidation guards (PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE env var + os.utime mtime bump) are jointly sufficient and individually redundant. Removing either alone leaves the other covering, so neither single-anchor mutant can kill. Both-at-once is not expressible under the single-anchor-per-mutant schema. Pending the expect:survived control-mutant feature.

mutants.name: score-any-nonzero-as-killed
mutants.why: the scoring arm's core claim — only exit 1 is KILLED. If this survives, any non-zero exit (timeouts, collection errors) could be miscounted as kills.

mutants.name: drop-baseline-control
mutants.why: the green-baseline positive control — a red baseline means the test was already failing, so a 'kill' is meaningless. If this survives, the suite does not actually require the baseline gate.

mutants.name: drop-per-mutant-target-lookup
mutants.why: the per-mutant target key must be consulted; dropping the lookup reverts to always using the manifest's top-level target, silently ignoring per-mutant overrides.

mutants.name: drop-unknown-key-refusal
mutants.why: unknown per-mutant keys must be refused; dropping the refusal silently accepts any key, leaving the class of 'silently-ignored field' defects this plan exists to close.

mutants.name: drop-filename-from-anchor-mismatch
mutants.why: the anchor-mismatch message must name the file searched; dropping it reverts to the uninformative message that made 100029's failure undiagnosable.

mutants.name: revert-pristine-cache-to-single-read
mutants.why: SAFETY-CRITICAL: the cache guard prevents reloading pristine content from an already-mutated sandbox file. Removing it causes the second mutant on the same target to load corrupted content as its baseline, scoring incorrectly.

mutants.name: revert-live-sha-guard-to-top-level-only
mutants.why: SAFETY-CRITICAL: the live-sha guard must cover every distinct target. Reverting to the top-level target only means mutations to per-mutant targets go undetected, weakening the central safety property.
